articles.title: How Is a Pencil Made?
articles.dek: You use one every day. But do you know where it comes from?
paras: Look in your pencil case. There is probably a pencil inside. You use it every day, but have you ever thought about it? How is a pencil made? Let's find out step by step.

First, the black part. People call it the "lead", but there is no lead metal in it. It is made of graphite and clay. Graphite is a soft, dark mineral. It leaves a grey line on paper. In a factory, the graphite is mixed with clay and water.
Next, the soft mix is pushed through a small hole. It comes out like long, thin strings. These strings are cut and dried. Then they are baked in a very hot oven. After that, they are hard and strong.

Now for the wood. Most pencils are made of cedar wood. Cedar smells nice, and it is easy to cut. The wood is cut into thin, flat pieces. Then small lines, called grooves, are cut into each piece. The black strings are put into the grooves.

A second piece of wood is glued on top, like a sandwich. A machine cuts the sandwich into pencils. One sandwich makes six to nine pencils! Many pencils have six sides, so they don't roll off your desk easily. Finally, the pencils are painted.

Pencils have a long history. More than 450 years ago, a lot of pure graphite was found in Borrowdale, in the north of England. At first, local people used it to mark their sheep! Later, it was used for writing and drawing.
So next time you write with a pencil, think about its long journey. It started as a dark stone under the ground. Now it is in your hand!

articles.title: Grandpa's Surprise Party
articles.dek: Grandpa is going to be seventy. Can the family keep the secret?
paras: Hi Leo, Grandpa is going to be seventy next Sunday! Mum wants to have a surprise party for him, so she asked me to help. We're going to invite all the family, but Grandpa can't know about it. Can you and Aunt Rosa come? Please don't tell him, because he talks to your mum every day! Love, Nina

Hi Nina, What a great idea! Of course we can come. Grandpa loves music, so I can play the guitar for him. My sister Ella is good at art, and she wants to make a big card. Where is the party going to be? I need to know because Mum is going to drive us there. Leo

Hi Leo, It's at our house. First, Dad is going to take Grandpa to the park for a walk. Then we're going to decorate the living room with balloons. After that, everyone is going to hide in the kitchen. When Grandpa opens the door, we're all going to shout "Surprise!" Please come at two o'clock, because they're leaving at half past two. Love, Nina

Hi Nina, The party was amazing! Grandpa opened the door, and his mouth fell open. He was really surprised, but he was very happy, too. He didn't stop smiling all afternoon. I played two songs on my guitar, but I forgot some words in the second one! Grandpa didn't mind. He sang with me, so nobody noticed. Leo

Hi Leo, Thank you for coming! Grandpa says it was his best birthday ever. After everyone left, he looked at Ella's card for a long time. Then he put it on the wall next to his bed. He wants you to teach him your songs, because he has an old piano at home. Please come again soon! Love, Nina

grammar.point: Linking words: and, but, so, because
grammar.rule: Linking words join ideas. and adds an idea, but shows a different idea, so gives a result, and because gives a reason. First, then and after that put actions in order.

articles.title: The Tent Was Too Small
articles.dek: Omar wanted to do everything himself. Then he packed the wrong tent.
paras: Last summer, Omar and his family went camping by a lake. Omar was very excited. He was fourteen, and he wanted to do everything himself. "I'm old enough to pack the car," he told his dad. "I'll get the tent from the garage."

They drove for three hours. When they arrived at the lake, Omar opened the tent bag. His face went red. It was his old tent from when he was ten, not the big family tent. "It's too small for four people!" said his sister Amira. The shops were too far away, and it was too late to drive home.
Dad had an idea. "The car is big enough for two people," he said. "Mum and I can sleep in the car. You two can have the tent." Omar felt very bad, but he said yes.

That night, it was very cold. Omar's sleeping bag was too thin, and he couldn't sleep. Then it started to rain. Water came in through a small hole in the tent. Amira woke up. "My feet are wet!" she cried. They weren't warm enough, and they weren't dry enough.
Omar didn't want to wake his parents. So he put his raincoat over the hole. He gave Amira his jumper. Then he told her funny stories until she laughed. Slowly, they both fell asleep.

In the morning, the sun came out. Mum made hot chocolate on a small cooker. Dad looked at the tent and smiled. "You weren't careful enough with the tent," he said, "but you were clever enough to fix the problem."
Omar laughed. Next time, he will check the bag before they leave. And he will pack the big tent!

grammar.rule: too + adjective means more than we want, so there is a problem: too small. adjective + enough means as much as we need: big enough. very only makes an adjective stronger: very cold.

kps.fact: Omar, fourteen, wanted to pack the car himself for a camping trip.
Omar packed his old small tent, not the big family tent.
It was cold and it rained, and water came through a hole.
kps.q: How did the water come into the tent?

kps.fact: Omar covered the hole with his raincoat and gave Amira his jumper.
kps.q: What did Omar put over the hole?

kps.fact: Dad said Omar was clever enough to fix the problem.
kps.q: What will Omar do next time?
opts: check the bag before they leave

mindmap.question: What went wrong on the camping trip, and how did Omar help?

summary.intro: Omar packs the wrong tent for a family camping trip.
summary.model: Omar packed a tent that was too small, so his parents slept in the car. The night was cold and wet, but Omar looked after his sister.

options.t: Omar packed his old tent, and it was too small for the family.
options.evidence: "It's too small for four people!" said his sister Amira.

options.t: On a cold, wet night, Omar helped his sister.
Dad said Omar was clever enough to fix the problem.
options.evidence: but you were clever enough to fix the problem.

options.t: Mum made hot chocolate in the morning.
options.why: True, but it is only a small detail.
options.evidence: Mum made hot chocolate on a small cooker.

options.t: The family caught a big fish in the lake.
Omar woke his parents in the night.
options.evidence: Omar didn't want to wake his parents.

speak.p: Would you like to go camping? Why or why not?
speak.hint: Try: 'I'd like to … because …' and 'It's too … for me.'

write.p: Look at the story idea: a family trip goes wrong. Write the story.
steps: Say how the problem was fixed.
